text: A farmer planted rice in rows so green
The finest little sprouts he'd ever seen
Each morning he would kneel to check their height
Too slow, too slow, he grumbled day and night
So out into the moonlit field he strayed
And tugged them all up higher, blade by blade
I helped our rice grow taller, he told his son
The boy ran out to see what he had done
Every single sprout lay withered, pale and dry
Their roots torn loose beneath the morning sky
Give it water, give it light, and take it slow
You cannot hurry what must grow
